newsitem.title: FRANCE: AGF results sow confusion, weaken shares.
newsitem.headline: AGF results sow confusion, weaken shares.

text.p: Shares in French insurer AGF closed lower on Thursday after it reported a nearly 50 percent jump in half-year profits and some analysts and traders attributed the price fall to concern over results in the autumn.
The shares closed down 3.5 francs or 2.46 percent at 138.5 francs.

"The quality of the results will be questioned by some," one London-based analyst said. "The profit improvement has come from capital gains and a reduction in the debt burden and not from the insurance business which is their core business," the analyst said.
But some others disagreed and said that the worry was misplaced.
"The results aren't easy to read but when one analyses them, taking out the exceptionals, one realises there's a strong increase in the operating profit," a Paris-based analyst said.
"I think they are good quality results," said another analyst, Patrick Leguil of Paris brokerage Transbourse.
Others attributed some of the drop in the share price to profit-taking after the shares' strong run-up ahead of the results.

AGF, which took big provisions last year to clean up its exposure to France's depressed property market, reported net attributable profit rose to 723 million francs from 487 million. The result was at the higher end of analysts' expectations.
AGF said the results were driven by a turnaround in its non-life business and a strong performance by its insurance activities outside France.
Non-life insurance added 364 million francs to profits, up by nearly 12 percent, reflecting better underwriting earnings.

Life insurance kicked in 131 million francs to earnings before exceptional items, down from 344 million for the same period in 1995, partly reflecting a sharp fall capital gains as well as the absence of a lucrative one-off contract distributed by the French post office.

Business was particularly strong outside France with AGF's Spanish unit swinging back to a profit of 27 million from a loss of 53 million. The Canadian unit had half-year earnings of 17 million compared with a loss of five million. And the Belgian unit's profits soared to 225 million from 125 million.

Sami Gotrane of Paris brokerage EIFB said the non-life technical margin rose by 18.6 percent. "That's very positive. There has also been a strong recovery in Spain," he said, adding he was looking for a full-year profit of 1.51 billion francs.
In life assurance, analysts said AGF turned in a respectable performance in face of severe margin pressure. "They have been able to limit the damage," said one analyst.

Losses from banking activities rose to 346 million compared with losses of 203 million a year earlier. But that reflected a 245 million franc addition to the general banking risks reserve to cover losses on future disposals.

One analyst said making the provision an addition to general banking risks reserve was a prudent accounting move which would boost shareholder equity and could be used for calculating AGF's solvency ratios.
Analysts were also encouraged by AGF's troubled property lending arm Comptoir des Entrepreneurs which more than halved its loss to 32.5 million francs from 67 million.
